# Pueue

![Pueue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nukesor/images/main/pueue-v2.0.0.gif)

Pueue is a command-line task management tool for sequential and parallel execution of long-running tasks.

Simply put, it's a tool that **p**rocesses a q**ueue** of shell commands.
On top of that, there are a lot of convenient features and abstractions.

Since Pueue is not bound to any terminal, you can control your tasks from any terminal on the same machine.
The queue will be continuously processed, even if you no longer have any active ssh sessions.

## Features

- Scheduling
  - Add tasks as you go.
  - Run multiple tasks at once. You decide how many tasks should run concurrently.
  - Change the order of the scheduled tasks.
  - Specify dependencies between tasks.
  - Schedule tasks to run at a specific time.
- Process interaction
  - Easy output inspection.
  - Send input to running processes.
  - Pause/resume tasks, when you need some processing power right NOW!
- Task groups (multiple queues)
  - Each group can have several tasks running in parallel.
  - Pause/start tasks by a group.
- Background process execution
  - The `pueued` daemon runs in the background. No need to be logged in.
  - Commands are executed in their respective working directories.
  - The current environment variables are copied when adding a task.
  - Commands are run in a shell which allows the full feature set of shell coding.
- Consistency
  - The queue is always saved to disk and restored on kill/system crash.
  - Logs are persisted onto the disk and survive a crash.
- Miscellaneous
  - A callback hook to, for instance, set up desktop notifications.
  - JSON output for `log` and `status` if you want to display info about tasks in another program.
  - A `wait` subcommand to wait for specific tasks, a group (or everything) to finish.
- A lot more. Check the -h options for each subcommand for detailed options.
- Cross Platform
  - Linux is fully supported and battle-tested.
  - MacOS is fully supported and on par with Linux.
  - Windows is fully supported and working fine for quite a while.

## What Pueue is **not**

Pueue is **not** designed to be a heavy-duty programmable (scriptable) task scheduler/executor.

The focus of `pueue` lies on human interaction, i.e. it's supposed to be used by a real person on some kind of OS.

Due to this, the feature set of `pueue` and `pueued` as well as their implementation and architecture have been kept simple by design!
Even though it can be scripted to some degree, it hasn't been built for heavy-duty work like hundreds of tasks!

## Installation

Pueue can be installed via your system's package manager, or by downloading prebuilt binaries from the [release page](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/releases).

## How to Use it

Pueue consists of two components:
- `pueued` - The daemon that runs in the background and manages your tasks
- `pueue` - The client used to interact with the daemon

### Basic Commands

                     This means that the command needs proper shell escaping.
                     The safest way to preserve shell escaping is to surround your command with quotes, for example:
                     pueue add 'ls $HOME && echo "Some string"'
  remove         Remove tasks from the list. Running or paused tasks need to be killed first
  switch         Switches the queue position of two commands. Only works on queued and stashed commands

                     By default, identical tasks will be created and enqueued, but it's possible to restart in-place.
                     You can also edit a few properties, such as the path and the command, before restarting.
  pause          Either pause running tasks or specific groups of tasks.

## Similar Projects

#### slurm

[Slurm](https://slurm.schedmd.com/overview.html) is a feature rich and widely used cluster management and scheduling system.
If you find yourself in the need for complex setups such as multiple worker pools or distributed nodes, slurm will be much better suited than Pueue.

#### GNU Parallel

A robust and featureful parallel processor with text-based joblog and n-retries. [GNU Parallel](https://www.gnu.org/software/parallel/parallel_tutorial.html) is able to scale to multi-host parallelization and has complex code to have deep integration across different tools and shells, as well as other advanced features. `Pueue` differentiates itself from GNU Parallel by focusing more on visibility across many different long running commands, and creating a central location for commands to be stored, rather than GNU Parallel's focus on chunking a specific task.

#### Pm2

[pm2](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/quick-start/) is a process management tool, whose focus is more on management of recurring and long-living tasks.
It seems to be quite mature and has a rich interface.

#### nq

A very lightweight job queue system which advertises no setup, maintenance, supervision, or otherwise long-running background processes. \
[Link to project](https://github.com/leahneukirchen/nq)

#### task-spooler

_task spooler_ is a Unix batch system where the tasks spooled run one after the other. \
Links to [ubuntu manpage](http://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/xenial/man1/tsp.1.html) and a [fork on Github](https://github.com/xenogenesi/task-spooler).

DELAY FORMAT:

    The --delay argument must be either a number of seconds or a "date expression" similar to GNU
    "date -d" with some extensions. It does not attempt to parse all natural language, but is
    incredibly flexible. Here are some supported examples.

    2020-04-01T18:30:00   // RFC 3339 timestamp
    2020-4-1 18:2:30      // Optional leading zeros
    2020-4-1 5:30pm       // Informal am/pm time
    2020-4-1 5pm          // Optional minutes and seconds
    April 1 2020 18:30:00 // English months
    1 Apr 8:30pm          // Implies current year

    wednesday             // The closest wednesday in the future
    4 months              // 4 months from today at 00:00:00
    1 week                // 1 week at the current time
    1days                 // 1 day from today at the current time

Restart failed or successful task(s).

By default, identical tasks will be created and enqueued, but it's possible to restart in-place. You
can also edit a few properties, such as the path and the command, before restarting.

          option).

          dependencies tasks may have

          Set the restarted task to a "Stashed" state. Useful to avoid immediate execution

          Restart the task by reusing the already existing tasks. This will overwrite any previous
          logs of the restarted tasks.
          
          This can also be enabled by default via the `restart_in_place` config option.

          `restart_in_place` configuration set to true

===== status --help =====
Display the current status of all tasks

Usage: executable status [OPTIONS] [QUERY]...

Arguments:
  [QUERY]...
          Users can specify a custom query to filter for specific values, order by a column
          or limit the amount of tasks listed.
          
          Syntax:
             [column_selection]? [filter]* [order_by]? [limit]?
          
          where:
            - column_selection := `columns=[column]([column],)*`
            - column := `id | status | command | label | path | enqueue_at | dependencies | start |
            end`
            - filter := `[filter_column] [filter_op] [filter_value]`
              (note: not all columns support all operators, see "Filter columns" below.)
            - filter_column := `status | command | label | start | end | enqueue_at`
            - filter_op := `= | != | < | > | %=`
              (`%=` means 'contains', as in the test value is a substring of the column value)
            - order_by := `order_by [column] [order_direction]`
            - order_direction := `asc | desc`
            - limit := `[limit_type]? [limit_count]`
            - limit_type := `first | last`
            - limit_count := a positive integer

cat > /tmp/test_status.py <<'PY'
import sys, subprocess, struct, socket, threading, os
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); from cbor import encode, decode
path="/home/agent/.local/share/pueue/pueue_agent.socket"
def run(state, extra_args=[]):
    try: os.unlink(path)
    except: pass
    s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM); s.bind(path); s.listen(1); s.settimeout(5)
    resp={"Status": state}
    payload=encode(resp)
    def serve():
        try:
            conn,_=s.accept(); conn.settimeout(5)
            def recv_exact(n):
                d=b""
                while len(d)<n:
                    c=conn.recv(n-len(d))
                    if not c: raise EOFError()
                    d+=c
                return d
            def recv_msg():
                hdr=recv_exact(8); ln=int.from_bytes(hdr,'big'); return recv_exact(ln)
            recv_msg(); conn.sendall(struct.pack(">Q", len(b"testversion"))+b"testversion")
            recv_msg(); conn.sendall(struct.pack(">Q", len(payload))+payload)
            conn.settimeout(1)
            try:
                while True: recv_msg()
            except: pass
            conn.close()
        except Exception as e: print("serve err",e)
        finally: s.close()
    import threading
    t=threading.Thread(target=serve,daemon=True); t.start()
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','-c','/tmp/pueue_test/empty.yml','status']+extra_args, cwd='/tmp', capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
    t.join(2)
    print("STATE",state)
    print("exit",r.returncode); print("stdout:\n",r.stdout); print("stderr:\n",r.stderr)

run({"tasks":{},"groups":{}})
run({"tasks":{},"groups":{"default":{"status":"Running","parallel_tasks":1}}})
run({"tasks":{},"groups":{"default":{"status":"Paused","parallel_tasks":0}}})

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EditMode { Toml, Files }
impl Default for EditMode { fn default() -> Self { EditMode::Toml } }
impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for EditMode {
    fn deserialize<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error>
    where D: Deserializer<'de> {
        // serde_yaml supports tagged enums; plain strings toml/files also.
        #[derive(Deserialize)]
        enum Repr {
            #[serde(rename = "toml")]
            Toml,
            #[serde(rename = "files")]
            Files,
        }
        // This will fail for sequence with expected tag message from inner? For probing compatibility we accept.
        match Repr::deserialize(deserializer) {
            Ok(Repr::Toml) => Ok(EditMode::Toml),
            Ok(Repr::Files) => Ok(EditMode::Files),
            Err(e) => Err(e),
        }
    }
}

path="/home/agent/.local/share/pueue/pueue_agent.socket"
state={"tasks":{},"groups":{"default":{"status":"Running","parallel_tasks":1}}}
responses=[{"Status":state},{"Success":"reset done"}]
# serve convo in this process
try: os.unlink(path)
except: pass
s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM); s.bind(path); s.listen(1); s.settimeout(10)
def serve():
    conn,_=s.accept(); conn.settimeout(10)
    def rex(n):
        d=b""
        while len(d)<n:
            c=conn.recv(n-len(d))
            if not c: raise EOFError()
            d+=c
        return d
    def rm():
        h=rex(8); return rex(int.from_bytes(h,'big'))
    def sm(b): conn.sendall(struct.pack(">Q",len(b))+b)
    rm(); sm(b"testversion")
    for resp in responses:
        try: req=rm()
        except: break
        sm(encode(resp))
    time.sleep(1); conn.close(); s.close()
threading.Thread(target=serve,daemon=True).start()
# Use script to allocate tty, feed y
proc=subprocess.Popen(["script","-qec","/tmp/original_executable -c /tmp/pueue_test/empty.yml reset","/dev/null"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
out,_=proc.communicate(input=b"y\n", timeout=10)
print(proc.returncode, repr(out))

        debug!(

            term_w,

# Agent Report

## Status
Reimplementation of the `pueue` 4.0.4 client (single binary, `pueue`) in Rust from black-box observation. It builds and passes extensive differential tests against the original binary for help/version/CLI errors, config errors, completions (all shells), status tables/JSON/query language, group/parallel, simple daemon commands, restart/edit/reset/wait/follow flows via a fake CBOR daemon.

## Key discoveries (from probing only, no source/decompilation)
- Binary is pueue client 4.0.4, clap-based. Help text wraps at 100 cols (needs clap `wrap_help`; a tiny local `terminal_size` crate is vendored under `vendor/terminal_size` and patched in Cargo.toml because that crate was not in the offline registry).
- Config: YAML `Settings{shared,client,daemon,profiles}`. Search paths: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pueue/pueue.yml` (or `~/.config/...`), then `./pueue.yml`. Explicit `-c`/`PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH` bypasses search logs. If no config found: error at `pueue/src/bin/pueue.rs:61`. Profile not found: line 55. Config parse/open errors: line 51.
- Daemon connection: unix socket default `<pueue_directory>/pueue_<username>.socket` (or `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, or `runtime_directory` config), secret file raw bytes, length-prefixed (u64 BE) handshake. **Protocol version = `0.31.1`** (brute-forced just before submission; set in `src/protocol.rs`). Messages are CBOR (ciborium) enums; responses: AddedTask, Edit, Status, Log, Group, Stream, Success, Failure, Close.
- Secret/cert errors at pueue.rs:91/:90; socket connect errors at pueue_lib client.rs:85; version handshake errors at :97/:99/:104.
- Status task model, TaskStatus (Locked/Stashed/Queued/Running/Paused/Done + TaskResult), table rendering (comfy-table-like), query language (columns/filters/order_by/limit with pest-style errors), wait polling (2s, status-change messages), follow (local `task_logs/<id>.log`, 500ms poll), edit (TOML default and `files` modes via `$EDITOR` + EditRestore), restart (Add vs in-place Restart, restart_in_place config), reset (Reset{Groups/All} + confirmation prompt when running/paused tasks exist).

## Known limitations / TODO
- `Log` non-empty response payload type and `AddedTask` response payload type were not fully reverse-engineered (deserialization oracle is masked by the client's "unexpected but valid message" fallback). Placeholder structs (`LogEntry{task,output}`, `AddedTaskResponse{message,task_id}`) are in `src/message.rs`; empty-log behaviour and Success/Failure handling match. A real pueued daemon's Log/AddedTask responses may therefore not decode. This is the main remaining task: discover those payload shapes.
- Protocol-version constant was updated to the discovered `0.31.1` at the last minute; the final release build was only smoke-tested after that change (handshake warning logic is just an equality check, so risk is low).
- TLS (TCP) mode: certificate-parse and connect errors are reproduced; actual TLS transport is bridged via the `openssl s_client` subprocess and is approximate (handshake error text may differ from rustls).
- Shell-escaping for `add --escape`, `max_status_lines` cell truncation, and the date `--delay` parser (interim-like natural language dates) are close approximations, not exhaustive.
- Tracing (`-vv`..`-vvvv`) subcommand/message Debug representations are reproduced for common commands; some rare paths may differ. Send-error file:line locations for a few helpers were inferred (e.g. get_state send at mod.rs:103).
- ` Stream` response variant and remote (non-local) log streaming are not implemented.

## Build
`./compile.sh` (cargo build --release --offline, copies binary to `./executable`).

## Tests performed
Differential harness scripts (fake CBOR daemon in Python under /tmp during development) compared the original and reimplementation for: all `-h`/`--help` output, version, clap errors/conflicts, completions for bash/elvish/fish/power-shell/zsh/nushell (all byte-identical incl. generated files), config/no-daemon error paths (130 cases), status/query/order/limit/JSON, group, wait, follow, restart, reset, edit (toml/files), simple Success/Failure/unhandled responses, verbose logging.
MD
./compile.sh 2>&1 | tail -3; ls -lh executable; ./executable --version; ./executable --help | head -3; ./executable status 2>&1 | head -4"}
